newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha slips from highs.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha slips from highs.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices slipped slightly in late business on Monday after showing early gains on the back of stronger crude oil futures, traders said.

June swaps traded at $187 and $187.50 and dealers said that fresh fob material which was available in northwest Europe and the Baltic Sea was exerting some downwards pressure on prices. Russian cargoes were valued by one end user at a discount of a dollar or so to the low of published quotes.
Physical markets were still said to be split between strong bids from traders for pipeline quality material, and numbers which were traded last week closer to $180 cif.
High paraffinic naphtha was valued at around $2.50 over the high cif of published quotes, and n+a was valued at least this much above the quotes, because of the strong showing on gasoline markets.
Turkey's Tupras said it had awarded a 22,000 tonne cargo of naphtha, loading on June 10-15, to Poten at $6 a tonne over fob Med quotes. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 8167
